raw_response:
I will start from what people around me do here and then adjust a little for my own land and budget. I have only farmed 2 years, so I will not make big changes all at once. On 10.1 mu, I will put more land into eggplant because that is my main crop this year, then keep some chili for cash flow, and keep wheat and maize so the whole year is not hanging on one vegetable price. We have well water, so I do not need to be stingy with irrigation, especially for eggplant and chili. For fertilizer, I will not cut too hard. If I save a few hundred yuan on fertilizer and lose yield, that is worse than putting a bit extra. I do look at nutrient balance now, not only urea. Wheat and maize I will run close to what local growers do, with wheat a bit heavier on base fertilizer and one more water at key stages. Eggplant and chili I will feed more because they carry fruit for a long time and remove a lot from the soil. For pests, vegetables need closer watching, so I will spray more times there; wheat and maize I will keep simpler. Tillage-wise, I will plough before wheat and most vegetable ground to turn the soil and manure in, and I will use rotary tillage for maize after the previous crop to save time and labor.
